bib.title: How Far Are We from Genuinely Useful Deep Research Agents?

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "How Far Are We from Genuinely Useful Deep Research Agents?" (FINDER and DEFT). Authors: OPPO AI Agent Team. Core contributors Dingling Zhang, He Zhu, Jincheng Ren, Kangqi Song, plus 12 contributors. Corresponding authors Wangchunshu Zhou and Jiaheng Liu (NJU address in the email). Preprint, arXiv:2512.01948v2 [cs.CL], dated 15-16 Dec 2025; no venue. The text names no affiliations beyond "OPPO AI Agent Team" and the OPPO and NJU email domains. Code and data: github.com/OPPO-PersonalAI/FINDER_DEFT. Local file: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/08-eval/sources/zhang-2025-how-far-we-genuinely-useful.pdf

COVERAGE: All 34 pages read. The extraction is 111,193 chars and I read all of it (main text, references skimmed, every appendix A-M). Figure content (the bar charts and radar plots) is garbled in extraction. The correlation matrix in Fig 6 is numeric and readable. The figures.py captions run returned nothing, so captions below come from the text. Appendix M ends mid-sentence ("As shown in the table below...") and the table it refers to is missing.

CORE CLAIM: Deep research agents (DRAs) fail less at understanding the task than at gathering, integrating and verifying evidence, and at planning that adapts. The most common single failure is fabricating plausible, unsupported content. The authors add a 100-task checklist benchmark (FINDER) and a 14-category failure taxonomy (DEFT) built by grounded-theory coding of agent reports.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Generation failures are the largest class, led by Strategic Content Fabrication.
 number: Generation 38.76%; SCF 18.95% (largest single category); Retrieval 33.10%; Reasoning 28.14%
 setup: share of coded failures across about 1,000 reports from 12 DRAs (9 used to build the taxonomy, plus WebThinker and OpenManus held out for saturation). FINDER = 100 tasks; 50 Chinese, 50 English. Labelled by LLM coders with human check. Who labelled the full set at scale is not stated.
 quote: "Reasoning (28.14%), Retrieval (33.10%), and Generation (38.76%)" and "Strategic Content Fabrication (3-5-SCF, 18.95%)"
 where: sec 4.4 and 4.5, p.9-10
 Caution: the intro says "over 39%" for generation and "over 32%" for retrieval, which does not match 38.76 and 33.10.
2. Within retrieval, the top failures are not fetching enough information and not verifying it.
 number: IIA 16.30%, VMF 8.72%, IHD 2.26%, IIF 2.91%, IRM 2.91%
 setup: same as above
 quote: "Insufficient External Information Acquisition (2-1-IIA, 16.30%)" ... "Verification Mechanism Failure (2-5-VMF, 8.72%)"
 where: p.9
3. Reasoning failures are comparatively low, but the agents are rigid planners.
 number: FUR 10.55%, LAD 11.09%, LAS 0.90%, RPS 5.60%
 quote: "Failure to Understand Requirements (1-1-FUR, 10.55%), Lack of Analytical Depth (1-2-LAD, 11.09%), Limited Analytical Scope (1-3-LAS, 0.90%), and Rigid Planning Strategy (1-4-RPS, 5.60%)"
 where: p.8
 The "reasoning resilience, not intensity" insight is asserted, not tested.
4. The taxonomy was checked for coder agreement with humans.
 number: Krippendorff alpha 0.7410-0.9152 by core category; checklist pass-rate alpha 0.8025 (OpenManus) and 0.8708 (WebThinker)
 setup: four experts versus Gemini 2.5-Flash on WebThinker and OpenManus outputs. App H says only 14 items (4+5+5) enter the alpha computation, with 1,000 bootstrap iterations.
 quote: "OpenManus 0.8005 0.7645 0.8960 0.8203 0.8025 / WebThinker 0.7410 0.9016 0.9152 0.8526 0.8708"
 where: Table 3, p.10; App H
 Construction ICR used three experts on samples of 24, then 54 records, with about 5 hours of discussion per round.
5. Failures cluster in correlated pathways.
 number: correlation FUR with CSD 0.67; IIA with SCF 0.53; LAD with IIA 0.73; SOD with RCP 0.75
 setup: Fig 6 correlation matrix of the 14 category counts; sample size, significance and unit of analysis not given
 quote: "(3) The Evidentiary Rigor cluster connects poor retrieval (2.1 IEIA) to "confident fabrications" (3.5 SCF)."
 where: p.10-11
6. Top-line agent scores differ by ranking depending on the lens.
 number: RACE overall: Gemini-2.5-Pro DR 50.95, Kimi K2 48.28, O3 DR 46.25. FACT citation accuracy (C.Acc.): O3 65.98, Gemini 57.09, Perplexity 5.25. Checklist pass: MiroFlow-EN 72.19, Tongyi 67.54, Kimi 66.59, Gemini 63.01, O3 57.52.
 setup: FINDER, RACE judged by Gemini 2.5 Pro against a Gemini-2.5-Pro DR reference report; FACT judged by Gemini 2.5 Flash
 quote: "Gemini 2.5 Pro Deep Research remains the top performer with an overall score of 50.95, followed by Kimi K2 (48.28) and O3 Deep Research (46.25)" and "MiroFlow-English achieves the highest score (72.19)"
 where: Table 1, p.6
7. A real fabrication and verification-failure example appears in the appendix, with no rate.
 number: none
 quote: "several references (e.g., PMC12396778, PMC11687125, PMC12021536) contained inaccessible URLs or linked to non-existent PMC entries" ... "the model incorrectly claimed that "all references have been cross-verified and meet the specified requirements.""
 where: App C (VMF case, OWL, task 27)
 Also App C RPS: the agent could not reach databases, kept its plan, and "relied on internally generated content to artificially fill each section".
8. The eval itself has holes, which the authors document.
 number: none
 quote: "Many academic publishers, government agencies, and commercial websites employ anti-scraping protections." / "In some instances, models generated URLs that do not correspond to real webpages."
 where: App M; "–" cells in Table 1 FACT columns (Kimi, O4-Mini, OWL)
 Also: "differences in absolute RACE scores across benchmarks hold limited interpretive value" (p.7), because RACE is relative to a reference report.
9. Positive score for taxonomy counts.
 number: S_i = |D| cos(E_i/|D| * pi/2)
 quote: "Si =|D| ·cos Ei/|D| · π2" (eq. 3, p.5)
 It is a bounded, monotone remap of error counts. The authors justify it by curvature, which is flat near zero errors.
10. FINDER stability.
 number: EN 45.54 +/- 0.43 vs ZH 44.49 +/- 0.20 overall RACE, three runs
 quote: "Overall 45.54 0.43 44.49 0.20"
 where: Table I.3, p.31
 Conflict: Table 1 gives the same system as 42.20 (EN) and 41.28 (ZH). Unexplained.

LIMITS
- Stated: FACT gaps from anti-scraping, fabricated URLs, timeouts. RACE scores are only relative to a reference.
- Unstated:
  - The reference report and the RACE judge are both Gemini 2.5 Pro (self-preference risk). Gemini also tops the table.
  - Failure shares come from LLM-assisted labelling. The agreement check covers only two agents and 14 items.
  - Table 1 Gemini row looks inconsistent: S1/S2/S3 are 89.80, 97.23, 89.80 but S_avg is 72.89. Other rows average correctly (e.g. Kimi 65.51), so this may be a typo.
  - Intro percentages disagree with the body (see claim 1).
  - Systems are not equal in scale or tooling: API models with "No tool integration", frameworks on different base models (OWL on o1, OpenManus on gpt-4o, MiroFlow on Claude-3.7-Sonnet).
  - Tasks are 100 PhD-style prompts from DRB, rewritten by 7 experts, with 419 checklist items. The checklists were refined by Gemini 2.5 Flash.
  - No test of the "reasoning resilience" claim.
  - Models and versions dated autumn 2025.

BUILDS ON: DeepResearch Bench (Du et al. 2025: tasks, RACE, FACT); grounded theory (Glaser & Strauss 1967; Makri & Neely 2021); seed concepts from Tang et al. (Agent KB, 2025) and Cemri et al. (Why do multi-agent LLM systems fail?, 2025); Krippendorff's alpha (Krippendorff 2018); cosine similarity (Salton et al. 1975); Seed1.5-Embedding. Related benchmarks named: GAIA, HLE, Mind2Web 2, DeepResearchGym, DeepScholar-Bench, DRBench, BrowseComp.

BEST-FIT SECTION IN 12-failure-modes.md (I read all 335 lines)
- The note covers: eval bugs, saturation, Goodhart, dev-set overfitting, contamination, judge drift, "Measuring the wrong thing", and eval debt. It cites no deep-research benchmark. It already has DR Tulu (rubric-reward mismatch) and the Terminal-Bench failure categorisation.
- Best fit in this note: "Measuring the wrong thing". Add a bullet that a relative, reference-scored judge (RACE) plus a citation check that cannot fetch pages (FACT) leave blind spots. Failures sit mostly in fabrication and unverified evidence, which a report-quality score barely shows. A second, smaller fit is the "Eval bugs look like agent bugs" table, row "Dropped rows": FACT "–" cells come from scraping blocks and fabricated URLs, so missing scores are an eval fault, not an agent one.
- Lacks: a failure taxonomy for long-form agents, and the fabrication rate share.
- Better-fitting notes:
  - 02-defining-correct.md "The failure taxonomy" (lines 129-175) is the strongest fit for the method. It teaches stable labels, stage ordering and coding traces. DEFT shows a grounded-theory build, saturation check on held-out agents and Krippendorff alpha. It would sharpen the rule "one label points to one fix" and "ordered by pipeline stage" (DEFT: reasoning -> retrieval -> generation).
  - 07-evaluating-rag-and-grounding.md (citation checks, "Pass the text, not the pointer") fits the fabricated citations / VMF / FACT claims.
  - 06-evaluating-agents.md "Agent-specific suites" (line 390, research suites) fits the benchmark and its checklist design. It already cites BrowseComp.
- Ledger row 2349 assigns the paper to 12-failure-modes.md, status "downloaded".

CODE: none worth keeping. The only formula is eq. 3 above.

FIGURES (captions from text, p. in PDF)
- Fig 1 (p.2): DRB query versus FINDER expanded query plus checklist. Shows what changed in one picture.
- Fig 2 (p.4): DEFT construction pipeline (LLM coder -> codebook -> refiner -> experts -> L3/L2/L1). Quick view of the method.
- Fig 3 (p.6): Level 1 and Level 2 failure categories radial/stage view. Garbled in extraction.
- Fig 5 (p.9): retrieval workflow with where failures 2-1..2-5 occur. Best candidate: it maps failures to stages in one view.
- Fig 6 (p.11): category correlation matrix; use it for the failure-pathway claim.
- Table 2 (p.8): 14-category list. Easiest to reuse as a table.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found.
- Figure and chart text is garbled; use the tables.
- Table 1 inconsistency (Gemini S_avg) and Table 1 vs Table I.3 MiroFlow RACE mismatch (42.20 vs 45.54).
- Intro's "over 39% / over 32%" versus body 38.76 / 33.10.
- Appendix M has a missing table.
- Section 4.5 refers to "2.1 IEIA" and "2.4 IIF" while Table 2 uses IIA, IIF = 2-3; the numbering of Fig 6 clusters is inconsistent (IIF is 2-3 in the list, "2.4" in the text).
- Typos such as "DEFT is built upon 100 expert-curated research tasks" (means FINDER).
